title: Braided Multisections and Akhmedov's Fake Quadrics
summary: We give handlebody decompositions of the complements of the cyclic multisections in $Σ_g\times S^2$ constructed in~\cite{AB}. The 2-handle framings are induced by the product coordinates. We compute the integral homology of the complements from their handle chain complexes, including the torsion subgroup of $H_2$. For the degree pairs $(3,3)$ and $(2,4)$, we specify surface diffeomorphisms inducing the maps on first homology prescribed in~\cite{AY} and recover the integral first homology groups $(\Z/3)^2\oplus\Z/(3m)$ and $(\Z/2)^2\oplus\Z/(4m)$, respectively, for $m\geq1$. For the symmetric $m=1$ sum, we also give a simultaneous surface diagram of the relative product attachments and identify their product framings with the surface framings. The resulting symplectic sums are aspherical and symplectically minimal, and have the rational cohomology ring of $S^2\times S^2$.

title: The residual map as a stratified fibration over the resonance arrangement
summary:
Given a stratum $\mathcal{H}(μ)$ of meromorphic one-forms on a Riemann surface with prescribed orders of zeros and poles, the residual map assigns to each differential the collection of its residues at the poles. In this paper, we prove that the residual map is a locally trivial topological fibration over each open flat of the stratification induced by the resonance arrangement.
  To give an algebro-geometric proof of this result, we introduce a refined compactification of the projectivized stratum $\mathbb{P}\mathcal{H}(μ)$, namely the moduli space of residue-aligned multi-scale differentials $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$. We prove that the projectivized residual map extends to $\operatorname{RAMS}(μ)$ as a stratified fibration over the projectivized resonance arrangement, thereby yielding a resolution of the projectivized residual map. This approach naturally extends to the analogue of the residual map for strata of $k$-differentials.
  Complementing the algebro-geometric approach, we also develop a flat-geometric point of view. In genus zero, each isoresidual fiber carries a canonical higher-dimensional analogue of a translation structure. These fibers admit a metric completion whose boundary has a modular interpretation in terms of the WYSIWYG compactification, for which we provide explicit local models. Isoresidual fibers admit a polyhedral cell decomposition whose geometry varies linearly with the underlying configuration of residues in period coordinates. Degenerations of these cells occur precisely when resonance conditions are satisfied, providing a geometric proof that the residual map is a stratified fibration. Finally, certain isoresidual fibers admit natural interpretations as Hurwitz spaces of branched covers, yielding unexpected homeomorphisms between moduli spaces of covers with prescribed ramification profiles.

title: Using Transformers to Generate 3-Manifold Triangulations
summary: Using dehydration signatures as an encoding, we train GPT-2-style transformers to generate triangulations of 3-dimensional manifolds. Our main runs each use approximately 3 exaFLOPs, spanning a 200 million parameter model trained on 60 million sphere triangulations to an 11 million parameter model trained on 1.1 billion sphere triangulations. The optimal model has 10 blocks, width 640 and generates dehydration signatures of closed manifolds of various topological types at a rate of 6.9%, 82% of which are spheres. To investigate how our method scales, we use the technique of IsoFLOP curves on 15-tetrahedron triangulations of the 3-sphere, over a compute range of 6 to 3000 petaFLOPs, and observe neural scaling behaviour. We extract a parameter scaling exponent of $α= 0.49$ ($[0.48, 0.50]$ stat, $\pm 0.02$ syst), and an optimal ratio of 234 tokens per parameter for training. In addition, we present a number of smaller experiments, including evidence that transformers are able to learn to count degree-one edges near-perfectly, but get progressively worse when counting edges with higher degrees.

title: Counting multigeodesics and the Selberg-Delange method
summary: We study the counting function $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$ for $m$-multigeodesics of length at most $x$ on a compact hyperbolic surface $X$ where $m$ is a positive integer. Building on the Selberg-Delange method, originally developed for counting integers with exactly $m$ prime factors in the interval $[1,x]$, we prove a large $x$ asymptotic for $\mathcal{P}^m(X,x)$. We show that for fixed $m$ as $x\to\infty$ the asymptotic is independent of the surface, whereas for $\frac{m}{\log x}$ bounded away from zero, the asymptotic depends on an infinite Euler product over the lengths of primitive closed geodesics. We also study the distribution of the function $ω_1$, defined on multigeodesics $Γ$ as $ω_1(Γ)=k-1$ for $Γ=(γ_1,...,γ_k)$ a $k$-multigeodesic. We show that as $x\to\infty$, the distribution of $ω_1$ in the set of multigeodesics of length $\leq x$ is close to that of a Poisson random variable with parameter $\log x$. Both of these theorems rely on studying the generating function of the random variable $ω_1$ which we relate to the Selberg zeta function.
